_spec.purpose: The caption variety engine, plus the corpus the comma ceiling will be computed from.
_spec.why: An opening move is the most repeatable thing in a caption, and a machine will find one that scores well and use it forever. Each shipped caption records its opening move and structure so the caption room can be told what is off the table.
_spec.comma_ceiling: NOT SET. It is computed from this product's first twenty shipped captions at ten percent below their measured mean, never copied from another product. config/parity_map.yaml carries the unblock condition; scripts/carousel/caption_check.py measures the rate every run.
_spec.doctrine: knowledge/carousel/CAPTION_CRAFT.md holds the menus this ledger rotates: ten opening moves, eight structures, five closing moves, and the anti-template law the critic judges by.
_spec.exclusions_handed_to_the_room: Opening moves, structures and closing substances, each off the table for the number of runs its own section of CAPTION_CRAFT.md states. The numbers are NOT written here. scripts/carousel/ledger_check.py reads all three from the doctrine with windows() and derives every stored list from them, so this field can never disagree with the rule. It used to read 'opening moves from the last 6 runs, structures from the last 3', which named two of the three windows, typed both, and left the closing window out of the contract entirely. A review bot on PR 252 found it beside the same defect in the gate. The room is told what is off the table before it writes, never after.

entry_schema.opening_move: one of the named moves in CAPTION_CRAFT.md
entry_schema.first_line: the actual first line, VERBATIM. Stored because the critic's real job is catching a sentence skeleton that survived a change of nouns, and it can only do that with the real lines in front of it
entry_schema.commas_per_100w: measured by caption_check.py, never typed. This is the corpus the ceiling will be computed from

_spec.recent_lists_note: These three lists are the exclusions handed to the caption room and they were hand-kept. On 2026-08-20 the fourth panel found structures_recent reading ["ledger", "pivot", "question and answer"] when the last three shipped structures were ["ledger", "two columns", "question and answer"], so it dropped a structure that IS off the table and held one that is not. Wrong in both directions from one hand edit. They are now recomputed from entries and are ordered OLDEST FIRST, matching the entries list, and scripts/carousel/caption_check.py should derive them rather than read them. That is an upgrade-lane change and it is written into this run's proposals.

entries.name_note: NORMALISED TO THE MENU at the eighth panel, which found all three names were coined freehand and appear nowhere in CAPTION_CRAFT.md. They read 'the flat statement of the finding', 'chronology, then the charge, then what the charge leaves out' and 'name the page the record was fetched from'. The caption did not change and did not need to: 'Texas authorized what was already driving' puts the old state of the world and the new one in one line, the body is ordered by date, and the close points at the record without asking for anything. All three of those are on the menu and none was excluded. A run that coins a name each day hands the next six runs an exclusion list that excludes nothing, which is how a variety engine quietly stops being one.

entries.first_line: Four abatements never got a vote. The item they all stood on failed first.
entries.critic_note: Two directors, opposed assignments. The winner opens on Brazoria's four abatements dying on a vote about none of them, which is a procedural fact a reader has no prior for, and only then widens to the seven. The loser opened on the count and narrowed, which is the shape three of the six shipped captions already use. caption_check reported first person on the winner because a period is a word boundary and I.3 matched \\bI\\b, and the gate was repaired in the upgrade lane rather than the caption reworded around a false positive. Round 4 renamed all three moves. They had been written freehand ('the procedural fact nobody expects', 'one case in full, then the pattern it belongs to', 'put the reader's own judgement on the instrument') and none of the three was on a CAPTION_CRAFT menu, which is exactly how they cleared an exclusion list that held all three. The choices were legal, the names were not, and a list can only exclude a name it shares.

entries.closing_move: ask the one question the decision leaves open
entries.first_line: The billion buys no building.
entries.critic_note:
TWO NAMING CALLS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The opening is named 'the number that is wrong', whose menu entry reads 'opens on a figure the reader will misjudge, then corrects it', and 'The billion buys no building' is exactly that. A judge read it as 'the correction', which is on the last six exclusion list, and the two doors are genuinely close. The distinction taken is that the correction's own example carries no figure and this line's subject IS the figure. The structure is 'ledger', what is known then what is not known then the size of the gap, which is the caption's actual order.

AND THE CLOSE REPEATS 08-25, WHICH THE EXCLUSION LIST COULD NOT HAVE PREVENTED. ledger_check derives closing_moves_recent from the entries BEFORE the newest, so while 08-25 was the newest its own closing move was excluded from the list by design and today's room was never handed it. Rolling it forward by hand made this file disagree with its own entries and turned shipped_check red on the already published 08-25 run, which is the gate working rather than failing. The room needs the lists derived INCLUDING the newest SHIPPED entry, with only the unshipped run's own entry held out. Upgrade lane, written down rather than hand edited.

entries.naming_call: THE CLOSING MOVE IS RECORDED AS THE ONE THE LAST THREE RUNS ALSO USED, and the reason is a hard gate rather than a lapse. brand.yaml sets linkedin_post.ends_with to engagement_question and caption_check hard fails a caption that does not end on one, so the close is a question whatever CAPTION_CRAFT's rotation would prefer. A rotation rule and a hard gate disagree here, and the disagreement is written down rather than resolved by quietly breaking one of them.

What the caption actually does is ask the one question the decision leaves open, and the date it names is in the sentence before. So this is the FOURTH run running on that move. entries.closing_move: name what happens next and when
entries.first_line: Open science has a closing date.
entries.critic_note: A SIXTH EDIT CAME IN ROUND 4 AND IT IS WHY THE WORD COUNT MOVED. The caption named no Texas place, which two scoring judges charged, so it gained 'The room it goes in is a new 20 MW data center in Round Rock.' from claim c22. That pushed it to 989 characters against brand.yaml's 300 to 900 band, so three things were cut to pay for it: the self-referential 'Nine frames read both guides side by side', the trailing 'to move data off' on the file systems sentence, and nothing else. The band is the reason the caption reads tighter, and a sentence about the deck itself was the right thing to spend. Two directors wrote to opposed assignments and the critic took B without spending its rewrite, with three surgical edits. It rejected A on two counts. A's close asked whether a NAIRR door opens to Frontera's users before October 1st, which imports a causal link no claim carries, and A ran one sentence skeleton six times inside a single caption, which is the anti-template law failing against the caption itself rather than against yesterday's. The three edits to B were to replace a close that was a riddle about a web page with one that names the next event, to split a compound sentence carrying two claims, and to change a definite article that over-asserted. A FOURTH EDIT CAME FROM A SCORING JUDGE RATHER THAN THE CRITIC. The caption said 'Horizon is next', which asserts a succession no fetched source states, and the deck had already REJECTED the one text that said it as a self-reported narrative. It now says the same center leads the construction project behind Horizon, which claim c21 carries. caption_check then caught 'centre' as British spelling in the repair. A FIFTH EDIT CAME FROM THE READER JUDGE IN ROUND 2 AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH REMEMBERING. The round 1 repair took the succession relation out of frame 9 and out of the caption BODY and left it standing as the caption's opening sentence, 'A successor is not a handover', which is the single line LinkedIn shows before the fold. A repair scoped to the list a judge happened to name is how a struck reading survives one surface further out, which this ledger already records from 2026-09-05. The opening is now 'Open science has a closing date', which c3 and c1 carry between them.

entries.first_line: Two ways to say when a patient goes home. A commercial tool wired into the health record. The hospital's own case managers.
entries.critic_note: REWRITTEN IN ROUND 4 AFTER THE SAME JUDGE ASKED TWICE. The shipped caption is the third version. The first opened 'Three clinicians compared a hospital's software against its own case managers' and was wrong twice in one line: c13's byline reads MD, BS, MD so CLINICIANS overstated it, and c5 calls the thing a commercial clinician-assisted tool rather than the hospital's own build. The second fixed both and still opened on a method summary, which the reader judge called the flattest first line in seventeen ledger entries. The third leads on the result and carries c6's reason in its second line. Two further fixes went in with it: 'At admission neither' was contradicted by the run's own c4, which says the case managers matched the exact date more often at admission, and the close asked 'How many stays sit inside that blank?', a question c10 answers and this run cut. THE WORD `actionable` ALSO SHIPPED IN VERSION TWO AND IS IN brand.yaml's banned_phrases. caption_check.py does not read that key, so nothing caught it and a judge did. It survives in the first comment only inside c6's verbatim quote, where the house rule says a quote is never touched. THE FIRST FILING OF THIS ENTRY USED FREEHAND MOVE NAMES, 'the result first', 'Turn and caveat' and 'name what the record cannot answer', and ledger_check refused all three: a freehand name cannot be excluded by a list of real ones, which is how three excluded moves shipped on 2026-08-25.
entries.carousel_no_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-10. This entry read carousel_no 18, the same number as the entry for 2026-09-08, and the sequence then jumped to 20. runs/carousel/2026-09-09/RUN_RECORD.md opens 'Carousel no. 19.', so 19 is the number that shipped. Candidate B asserted 'That list is not in the public file', an absence no document in the record establishes, and its first paragraph put a car with no brake pedal next to the Office of Defects above the fold with the defusal below it. Candidate A published 'paid', which appears in NO claim: c7 says commercial deployment and c12 says putting passengers in it, and the word was building an implicit contrast with Zoox's exemption that no claim supports. BOTH DEFECTS WERE ALREADY RENDERED ONTO THE COVER when the critic found them, along with c10's stripped qualifiers, and all three were fixed on the frame as well as in the copy. The critic also found that this ledger's own rolling exclusion lists had drifted from the entries beneath them and mis-briefed the room. They are DERIVED now.

entries.closing_move: Ask the one question the decision leaves open.
entries.first_line: The State Board of Education adopted a money class to match House Bill 27.
entries.critic_note: THE CRITIC FOUND A REAL LEDGER DEFECT RATHER THAN A PROSE ONE, and it is the reason this entry's opening and closing moves are the ones they are. Both candidates opened on the object and closed by asking the question the decision leaves open, and both moves were inside their own exclusion window. The caption also asserts one universal, None of them, and quantifiers.json names the six-term set it is over rather than leaving a reader to trust it. AFTER ROUND 1 the post lost two sentences the record did not carry, a graduation requirement c9 calls a curriculum requirement, and an effective date the motion asked for rather than the board settled, and the counts here were re-measured off the file. AFTER ROUND 2 the first line names the board and the bill it matches rather than compressing c6 to a bill number, and the universal over the release's closing words came out because the release's own sentence says invest. THE ROUND 3 INTEGRITY JUDGE READ THE FIRST LINE AS 'THE WHO' RELABELLED. The line names the board and the bill, then the post turns on what the adopted text asks for against what the bill asked for, which is the before and after the move name records. The judge's reading is kept here so the next critic can decide it with both in front of them.
entries.move_note: Named off CAPTION_CRAFT.md's own menus rather than freehand. ledger_check refuses a move name that is not on a menu, because a name nobody else uses cannot be excluded by a list of real ones, which is how three excluded moves shipped on 2026-08-25. The caption opens on what House Bill 27 asked for and turns to what the adopted text actually says, it runs what is known then what is not then the size of the gap, and it ends on the question the adoption leaves open.
